answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by treating reputation like an orchard rather than a field of annuals: each identity must grow a long-lived tree of completed, independently verified work, and the fruit — a trust signal — ripens only after seasons of consistent performance. A periodic pulse check prunes dead branches: identities that go silent or behave inconsistently lose their fruit. Planting a thousand fake orchards costs a thousand seasons of real work, while an honest agent tends one tree and harvests steadily.
